body:
Split out of **#508** (7th attempt rejected at sign-off on reviewability — one 44-file /
14,117-line cross-plane patch). This is **seam (ii)** of five: proposal 0016's decision 7,
landed on its own so the record-shape change to the object model is reviewable apart from the
multipart protocol that motivates it.

## What

`InodeRecord.chunk_map` graduates from a flat list to **`Flat | Segmented`**:

- flat stays exactly as it is today (`crates/core/src/metadata.rs:268`,
  `pub chunk_map: Vec<ChunkRef>`) and existing records keep decoding byte-identically;
- segmented carries a group identity plus `seg:<group-nonce>:<epoch>:<index>` segment records
  and their `seggrp:` reservation;
- a segmented map cannot be published in one batch, so it gets its own **staged publication**:
  write the segments, then flip the root (0016 decision 7, `:2280`, designed *with* decision 4's
  staged-obligation machinery as one pattern family);
- **one shared resolver**, and *every* `.chunk_map` consumer goes through it.

## Why

The launch requirement is objects **over 10 GiB**, and a chunk map is one JSON value. Working
the arithmetic (0016 `:218-232`): a `ChunkRef` encodes to ~131 B–~302 B, so the inherited
100 KB backend value ceiling at 2× headroom holds only **165–381 chunks — about 165–381 MiB**
of object at the 1 MiB default chunk size. That is *below* the 5 GB single-PUT ceiling, not
above it; even 13–32 MiB chunks reach only ~5–12 GiB, traded against gateway memory. **The flat
map is the binding ceiling for ordinary PUT as well as for multipart** — which is why this slice
stands on its own and lands first.

## Scope

- the `Flat | Segmented` record shape, the `seg:` / `seggrp:` records and their key helpers
  (`crates/core/src/metadata.rs`);
- staged segment publication and the root flip;
- the shared resolver, and **every** consumer routed through it — the gateway read path plus
  `crates/custodian/{gc,restore,scrub,reconstruction,rebalance}.rs`. This is not optional
  hygiene: #508's 4th attempt shipped a resolver used only by the read path while
  `crates/custodian/src/gc.rs` and `restore.rs` still iterated `record.chunk_map` directly, so a
  restore pass stranded and a later GC pass deleted a **live, committed** segmented object's
  fragments;
- the living architecture docs for the new record class
  (`docs/design/architecture/06-runtime-view.md`, `08-crosscutting-concepts.md`) — the
  docs-currency rule makes this a merge requirement in the slice that lands the change.

## Out of scope

- **FU-1 (#628)** — graduating the shape to an ADR is architecture-board authority, not this
  slice's, and not a model's to author;
- **FU-5 (#632)** — part-record segmentation (the same machinery one record class down);
- the multipart records and commit protocol, and the S3 verbs.

## Open point for the board (blocks nothing in this slice, but must be settled in it)

0016's decision 7 requires an **independent** segment-group nonce with a `seggrp:` reservation
(`:493-526`), while its implementation summary still equates the group to the upload id
(`:2318`). The editorial correction is tracked with #628; this slice must implement the
independent nonce (the later, corrective rule), not the upload-id spelling.

## Acceptance

- an object above the flat ceiling round-trips **byte-identical**, and its published `inode:`
  value stays **within the 100 KB value ceiling** (today the value simply grows past it — that
  is the red);
- a segmented object survives a full custodian reconcile step with its fragments intact
  (GC does not reclaim them, restore does not strand them);
- pre-existing flat records decode unchanged (byte-identity test);
- `cargo xtask ci` green.

## Reference

- Proposal 0016 decision 7 (`docs/design/proposals/draft/0016-multipart-commit-protocol.md:2280`),
  the object-ceiling arithmetic `:218-232`, the map value ceiling `:1043-1060`, and the
  implementing-slices summary `:2673-2691`.
- Successor to ADR-0047's flat-only record shape (see #628).
- Part of #508 / epic #513.

milestone.title: 0.1 Alpha
milestone.description: First tagged release (Alpha). Scheduled after the two production-metadata milestones complete: #14 (Metadata Store FoundationDB) and #5 (M4 — Production metadata backend) — i.e. after the FDB go/no-go (#442) records go, the default flips to FDB, and TiKV development stands down (#443). No due date yet; it follows those two. Starts empty as the release marker.

title: core: segmented chunk map (0016 decision 7) — Flat | Segmented + seg:/seggrp: records + one resolver for every consumer
